articles.title: Relembre histórias de moradores que viveram '15 minutos de fama' | G1
articles.standfirst: Para celebrar os 15 anos das páginas locais do g1 nas áreas de cobertura da TV TEM, reportagem especial reúne histórias de moradores do interior de SP que ganharam fama nacional.
articles.summary: Para celebrar os 15 anos do g1, relembramos trajetórias marcantes de moradores que viralizaram e transformaram suas vidas nas áreas de cobertura da TV TEM.
articles.body:
Relembre histórias que viveram seus ‘15 minutos de fama’ na área de cobertura da TV TEM — Foto: g1

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Quem não conhece a expressão popular “15 minutos de fama”? A frase usada para explicar casos de pessoas que alcançaram a fama de forma repentina não poderia ser mais atual em tempos de redes sociais e conteúdos virais. E muitas dessas histórias se transformaram em pautas jornalísticas.

Nesta quarta-feira (25), as páginas do g1 nas regiões de Bauru e Marília, Itapetininga e região, São José do Rio Preto e Araçatuba e Sorocaba e Jundiaí completam 15 anos. E para marcar e comemorar a data, confira histórias de 15 moradores dessas regiões que viveram os seus 15 minutos (ou mais) de fama.

O marco inicial da cobertura local foi em 25 de novembro de 2011, quando os sites regionais nas áreas de cobertura da TV TEM, afiliada da Rede Globo, entraram no ar, como parte do projeto de expansão do portal iniciado em 2010. Mais recentemente, em 31 de agosto de 2025, Presidente Prudente também passou a contar com uma página local, ampliando a presença do g1 no interior paulista.

Abaixo, relembre personagens que viralizaram e tiveram suas histórias conhecidas em todo o país por meio das reportagens do g1 em cada uma das regiões de cobertura da TV TEM.

Em 2016, uma adolescente de 11 anos de Jaú (SP) conquistou milhares de brasileiros com sua história de vida. Conhecida como Careca TV , Lorena Reginato dividiu com internautas momentos da luta contra o câncer no cérebro durante o tratamento. A jovem ultrapassou a marca de 1 milhão de inscritos no YouTube e ganhou uma legião de fãs.

Morando em Bauru, ela contou ao g1 como vive atualmente: "Me formei, estou tendo aula de paranatação e evoluindo na fisioterapia. Ganhei medalha em um festival de paranatação e agora estou treinando para ir em campeonato de natação".

Em relação ao amor que recebeu na época, Lorena revisita o sentimento que teve ao ser amada pelo Brasil: "Com certeza foram dias muito felizes, às vezes nem cai a ficha, sabe? Conheci pessoas maravilhosas que sigo a amizade até hoje", ressalta.

Dez anos após sucesso como ‘Careca TV’, youtuber mirim que venceu câncer celebra nova fase — Foto: Reprodução/Paulo Piassi/g1

Em 2018, a frase “ É verdade esse bilete ”, foi o terceiro meme mais buscado no Google. A autoria ida frase é do Gabriel Lucca, que na época tinha 5 anos. Aos 14 anos, o menino que repercutiu nas redes sociais continua morando em Bocaina (SP) e estuda em período integral.

“Na época o Gabriel tinha 5 anos, hoje está com 14 anos. A aparência mudou bastante, antes uma criança e hoje um adolescente. O Gabriel se destaca na escola pelo seu raciocínio e habilidade em determinadas matérias. Está se preparando para o futuro e já sonha com a profissão e faculdade”, afirma a mãe Geovana.

Segundo Geovana, Gabriel sonha em fazer faculdade de Direito e ainda é reconhecido pela história do 'bilete'. "Na escola, durante uma matéria escolar apareceu o 'bilete' como estudo. Ele conta que os amigos de sala ficaram empolgados com a matéria e com a foto estampada no livro didático escolar."

Gabriel Lucca, que viralizou com o meme "É verdade esse bilete", surgiu em agosto de 2018 quando tinha apenas 5 anos — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Em 2025, uma missa viralizou por um motivo curioso . Uma criança subiu no altar para realizar sua prece e fez um pedido inusitado ao padre Luiz Henrique de Araújo: que sua família fosse abençoada e que o Palmeiras não fosse campeão mundial. Assista ao vídeo abaixo.

Ao g1 na época, o padre de Tupã (SP), que torce para o time, confessou ter ficado surpreso: "Eu como palmeirense, não foi fácil escutar aquele pedido de oração, confesso. Eu não sabia o que dizer, então preferi ficar quieto num primeiro momento".

Padre Luiz Henrique explicou a reação ao pedido do menino durante a missa em Tupã — Foto: TV TEM/Reprodução

O padre, então, negou o pedido à criança : "Eu sou palmeirense e o menininho falou isso, que o palmeirense não tem a mundial. Eu falei: 'Essa prece não vai ser atendida'", brincou ele. Apesar de rivais na torcida, a brincadeira rendeu bons momentos entre o pároco e o pequeno fiel, que chegaram a ver os jogos do Palmeiras na competição juntos.

Apelidada como “ Vampira do Drift ” , uma bauruense deu o que falar – a la Velozes e Furiosos – em agosto de 2026. O acidente com a motorista Ana Beatriz Godoy, de 25 anos, no dia 18 de agosto, no centro da cidade, ganhou repercussão nacional nas redes sociais.

Ana Beartiz Godoy, a Vampira do Drift viralizou nas redes sociais — Foto: Bryan Assis

Foram essas imagens registradas por câmeras de segurança, inclusive, que abriram as portas para que ela virasse "influencer".

Carro entra em loja e estaciona em vaga do estabelecimento após batida entre as ruas Marcondes Salgado e Antônio Alves, em Bauru — Foto: Reprodução/Câmera de Segurança

Na época, ela se impressionou com a repercussão: “Eu não imaginei que fosse chegar nessas proporções. Pensei que no máximo ia dar uma viralizada, com 50 mil visualizações, mas eu nunca imaginei que fosse ser chamada para reportagens, publicidades, e que fosse repercutir no Brasil inteiro”, disse ao g1.

Em 2025, o estudante de medicina e coletor de lixo Guilherme da Silva Mazini, de Presidente Prudente (SP), conquistou milhares de seguidores nas redes sociais ao compartilhar a rotina intensa de “corres” para realizar o sonho de atuar na área da saúde.

O jovem chamou a atenção na web ao mostrar como equilibrava a faculdade em período integral, cursada por meio do Financiamento Estudantil (FIES), com o trabalho noturno na limpeza urbana, na escala 6x1. Durante a semana, ele precisava sair 10 minutos mais cedo das aulas, que iam das 7h30 às 17h10, para conseguir assumir o turno na coleta às 17h e seguir no batente até por volta da meia-noite.

Guilherme Mazini, 24 anos, trabalha como coletor de lixo há três anos e começou a estudar medicina em 2025 — Foto: Guilherme Mazini/Arquivo pessoal

Ao g1 , Guilherme contou que atualmente está no quinto semestre, encaminhando-se para a metade do curso, e segue conciliando os estudos com o trabalho. Apesar da rotina cada vez mais corrida e desafiadora, ele celebra o carinho que recebe nas ruas.

“O que é gratificante é o reconhecimento. Quando passo nos lugares, as pessoas me chamam de ‘Doutor’ e querem saber como estou, isso com certeza vale a pena demais. Essa história está presente no meu dia a dia e estará marcada pela minha vida inteira. Conseguir chegar e mostrar que é possível faz com que as pessoas se inspirem a correr atrás dos seus sonhos”, destaca.

O jovem Moisés Carlos dos Santos, de 18 anos, morador de Presidente Epitácio (SP), viralizou nas redes sociais ao transformar prateleiras de supermercado em obras de arte . Em janeiro de 2026, ele contou ao g1 que, logo no primeiro dia na nova função, percebeu que sua relação com as gôndolas seria diferente.

"Eu via brilhos nas prateleiras. Sentia que eu poderia mexer nelas [gôndolas], porque antigamente era só um produto lá. Aí pedi para os gerentes e comecei uma das minhas histórias nas redes sociais. Isso foi surgindo com o tempo", relembrou.

Jovem repositor de Presidente Epitácio viraliza ao transformar prateleiras de supermercado em 'obras de arte' — Foto: Moisés Carlos dos Santos/Arquivo Pessoal

Ainda de acordo com Moisés, ele realiza um planejamento visual antes de cada montagem, reunindo ideias e criando layouts que transformam latas, caixas e garrafas em figuras organizadas.

Um clique especial feito com drone em uma visão Panorâmica do Caminho dos Devotos — Foto: Raul Muniz

O empresário Agesner Monteiro criou o Caminho dos Devotos , no km 444 da Rodovia Assis Chateaubriand, entre Presidente Prudente e Regente Feijó (SP), em agradecimento pela vida e saúde do filho Ravi, hoje com seis anos. Em 2020, aos cinco meses, o bebê sofreu uma queda da cama, teve traumatismo cranioencefálico grave e passou por uma cirurgia de emergência, mas se recuperou sem nenhuma sequela.

Peregrinos visitam o Caminho dos Devotos, entre Presidente Prudente e Regente Feijó, no interior paulista — Foto: Agesner Monteiro/Arquivo pessoal

Inaugurado em outubro de 2020, o espaço conta com uma capela, reúne esculturas de cerca de 10 metros de altura e recebe aproximadamente 10 mil visitantes por mês. Em abril de 2026, quando o local tinha 11 imagens prontas e outras sete em produção, o empresário falou ao g1 sobre o propósito do santuário.

“O significado para mim de tudo isso é uma satisfação. É prazeroso você ver as pessoas se emocionando naquele lugar, orando. É um lugar que só tem coisas boas”, completa o idealizador.

Morador cria espaço de devoção com santos gigantes próximo de rodovia no interior de SP em homenagem ao filho — Foto: Agesner Monteiro/Arquivo pessoal

Em 2019, o motoboy Afonso Saraiva Leão Neto, na época com 19 anos, viralizou nas redes sociais ao dançar com integrantes de um “trenzinho da alegria”. Ele voltava da última entrega de açaí em São José do Rio Preto (SP) quando parou no cruzamento das avenidas Governador Adhemar Pereira de Barros com a Adolfo Lutz e decidiu entrar na dança. ( Assista no vídeo abaixo ).

O flagrante feito pela estudante Bárbara Horrana Garcia repercutiu rapidamente e recebeu milhares de comentários, entre eles, do influencer e comediante Whindersson Nunes. Ao g1 na época, Afonso disse que tinha acabado de fazer a última entrega , era sábado à noite e estava feliz, por isso resolveu descer da moto e dançar com o grupo. Ele também comentou sobre ter viralizado.

“Estou achando engraçado. Do dia para a noite ficou famoso e estou achando bacana, bem interessante a repercussão. Vi que vários perfis compartilharam, brincaram com a situação e que viralizou”, disse.

Quem também chamou a atenção com a dança foi o capitão da PM Vander Luís Duarte dos Santos, de Araçatuba (SP). Durante uma live realizada pela corporação para arrecadar alimentos para três entidades durante a pandemia de Covid-19, o Capitão Duarte arrasou no “passinho” dos anos 1980 . ( Veja abaixo ).

A dança durou pouco, mas foi o suficiente para viralizar e ser compartilhada até no perfil do Padre Fábio de Melo, que tem mais de 25 milhões de seguidores. Na ocasião, Duarte conversou com o g1 e falou sobre o seu interesse pela dança.

“Eu gosto muito de Michael Jackson e James Brown. Eu costumo dançar nas festas e em casa. Na hora do trabalho, levamos a sério, mas quando estamos de folga, precisamos fazer o que gostamos.”

Já no caso do Pedro Henrique Biondo Matias, de Orindiúva (SP), foi o som do berrante que fez com que ele ficasse conhecido em todo o país. Em quase três anos de viagem, Pedro cruzou 16 países e percorreu cerca de 60 mil quilômetros pelas Américas acompanhado do cachorro Bastião e de um berrante. A jornada se encerrou em 2026, na Festa de Barretos em agosto.

Pedro Berranteiro ao lado do cão Bastião — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Conhecido como “Berranteiro das Américas”, ele acumula mais de 1 milhão de seguidores nas redes sociais . Em 2023, Pedro decidiu deixar a vida estável e emprego na área de engenharia civil para seguir o sonho de conhecer o continente americano e honrar as tradições de antigos peões e tropeiros. De volta da jornada, ele conversou com o g1 .

“Eu voltei uma pessoa diferente, aprendi a ser mais humilde e vi que a gente depende muito da ajuda das pessoas todos os dias. Eu sabia que ia ter que abrir mão de várias coisas, mas valeu a pena. Eu buscava motivação para viver e encontrei.”

Em 2014, o estudante Nilson Meira, de Votorantim (SP), na época com 10 anos, viralizou na internet após não conseguir segurar uma crise de risos durante uma oração transmitida ao vivo por um canal de TV comunitária. (Assista ao vídeo abaixo).

Coroinha desde pequeno, o garoto participava da reza da "Ave Maria" quando um amigo ao lado deu uma cutucada em suas costas — o suficiente para desencadear as gargalhadas que renderam milhões de visualizações nas redes sociais. Apesar de ter enfrentado críticas e bullying no início, o jovem contou com o apoio da família e da paróquia para superar a repercussão com bom humor.

Em entrevista ao g1 em 2018, Nilson mostrou que havia tirado de letra a fama repentina.

“Me incentivou a ser aquilo que eu sou, não me importando em dar risada e ser alegre. Muitas pessoas falaram que eu era o bobo alegre, mas é melhor ser alegre e feliz do que aquela pessoa triste, sem dar risada e fechada. Vou fazer o quê? Virei o ‘gordinho do Ave Maria’”, brincou.

Nilson ficou conhecido como o 'gordinho do Ave Maria' — Foto: Carlos Dias/G1

O estudante de engenharia mecânica Gustavo Machado, de 23 anos, viralizou nas redes sociais ao construir uma montanha-russa no quintal de casa, em Caieiras (SP). O projeto caseiro, iniciado quando ele tinha 17 anos e que exigiu pelo menos dez protótipos até funcionar com segurança, rendeu milhões de visualizações na internet. (Assista ao vídeo abaixo).

O hobby acabou virando profissão. Morando atualmente em Sorocaba (SP), Gustavo foi contratado para atuar na supervisão de montagem da montanha-russa gigante do Cacau Park, em Itu (SP) — atração de 55 metros de altura que atinge 120 km/h e é considerada a maior e mais rápida da América Latina.

Ao g1 , o jovem contou que a visibilidade abriu portas até fora do país e o levou recentemente à IAAPA Expo, uma feira internacional de parques em Orlando, nos Estados Unidos.

“Cheguei a receber mensagens de engenheiros também em decorrência da matéria do g1, e me possibilitou ter ainda mais essa troca de informações. É uma grande felicidade ver algo que começou pequeno no meu quintal chamando a atenção de quem projeta as maiores atrações do mundo”, celebra.

Estudante de engenharia, Gustavo Machado, viralizou ao construir uma montanha-russa no quintal e hoje trabalha na construção do brinquedo no Cacau Park, em Itu (SP) — Foto: Gustavo Machado/Arquivo pessoal

O comediante Wilson de Oliveira Lopes, mais conhecido como Lopes Dilo, ganhou o apelido de “Neo de Jundiaí” após o público notar sua semelhança com o astro de Hollywood Keanu Reeves. Morador de Jundiaí (SP), ele começou a ser comparado ao ator ao publicar vídeos de humor na internet, em 2017, e decidiu investir na carreira de sósia profissional.

Lopes Dilo à esquerda e Keanu Reeves em 'Matrix Resurrections' à direita — Foto: Arquivo pessoal - Reprodução

Com cabelo na altura dos ombros e barba desenhada, ele passou a ser contratado para eventos caracterizado como personagens icônicos do ator, como Neo, de “Matrix”, e John Wick. Depois da reportagem publicada pelo g1 , em 2023, a visibilidade cresceu e rendeu convites para podcasts, rádios, talk shows e participações em emissoras de TV.

Ao g1 , Lopes Dilo destacou que a fama como sósia ajudou a abrir espaço para a comédia.

“Essa matéria foi muito significativa para a divulgação do meu trabalho, me rendeu muitos seguidores e abriu portas para eu mostrar meu verdadeiro objetivo: revelar meu talento humorístico. Tive oportunidade depois da matéria de ser convidado para renomados Podcasts, rádios ,entrevistas em talk shows e até participar de eventos em emissoras de TV”, afirma.

Lopes Dilo também é apresentador de programa de entrevistas no YouTube — Foto: Reprodução/YouTube

Em 2016, Paulo Gabriel da Silva Barros, apelidado de Paulinho Gigante, e Katyucia Lie Hoshino Barros, de Itapeva (SP), ganharam repercussão no Brasil e no exterior ao entrarem para o Guinness Book, o livro dos recordes, como o menor casal do mundo. Juntos, eles somam 1,81 metro de altura — ele mede 90 centímetros e ela, 91 centímetros. (Assista ao vídeo abaixo.)

A história dos dois, que se conheceram pelo extinto Orkut em 2006 e oficializaram o casamento em setembro de 2016, conquistou o público pela leveza com que encaravam a rotina em uma casa adaptada e pela viagem a Londres, na Inglaterra, para receber o certificado oficial do recorde.

Ao g1 na época, o casal celebrou a chance de mostrar o dia a dia ao público: “Entrar no livro dos recordes é uma oportunidade para mostrarmos um pouco da nossa rotina, mostrar quem a gente é, e também representar o Brasil e Itapeva no Guinness”, destacaram.

De Itapeva, 'menor casal do mundo' fala sobre preconceito contra pessoas com nanismo — Foto: Facebook/ Reprodução

Em 2025, o gato Frajolito, de Tietê (SP), concorreu ao prêmio iBest na categoria "Pets" após viralizar nas redes sociais com um vídeo em que aparecia usando o “trono” . Na época, o tutor Mailson Maciel contou ao g1 que não imaginava que as publicações teriam tanta repercussão, chegando a ultrapassar sete milhões de visualizações.

O felino foi resgatado ainda recém-nascido pela família. "Escutamos o miado de um filhote de gatinho. Ele estava abandonado e bem fraquinho, com os olhos fechados. Creio que ele tinha entre quatro e seis dias, e não pensamos duas vezes em levar para casa e cuidar dele", relembrou.

Curioso desde os primeiros dias de vida, Frajolito conquistou a internet com suas "gatices", mas o grande destaque veio com a habilidade inusitada de fazer xixi no vaso sanitário — espaço que hoje é exclusivo dele na casa.

Atualmente, o perfil do tutor ao lado do gato reúne cerca de 200 mil seguidores, com vídeos que alcançam entre 60 mil e 90 mil visualizações.

articles.summary: Escola Estadual de Ensino Médio Joaquim Nabuco completou 100 anos em agosto deste ano.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Tupanciretã luta para se reerguer. São milhões de reais investidos na reconstrução do município da Região Central do Rio Grande do Sul atingido por uma supercélula na última sexta-feira (20) , com toneladas de entulhos recolhidos e ainda 19 mil pessoas fora de casa . A tempestade deixou 5 mortos .

Um dos locais que foi severamente danificado foi a Escola Estadual de Ensino Médio Joaquim Nabuco, instituição centenária localizada no município que havia passado por reforma completa recentemente.

"A gente reformou toda ela. Trocamos piso, arrumamos toda parte só faltava a rede elétrica. O restante todo nós tínhamos organizado. Quando eu consegui sair da minha casa, eu só pensava em vir na escola. A imagem era que está destruída a nossa escola", lamenta a diretora da escola Daiane Dutra dos Santos.

A escola completou 100 anos em 19 de agosto deste ano e foi homenageada pela Câmara Municipal da cidade.

A prefeitura de Tupanciretã suspendeu as aulas no município após todas as escolas da cidade registrarem algum tipo de dano. Além da Joaquim Nabuco, a tempesteda avariou a Escola Estadual de Ensino Fundamental (EEEF) Antônio Silveira, a EEEF Protásio Lima de Moraes e o Instituto Estadual de Educação Mãe de Deus.

Em todas as edificações, houve danos nos telhados e esquadrias. A diretora relata o que encontrou quando chegou no local, após o evento climático.

"Quando cheguei, não tinha como entrar, porque era muita árvore, muita fiação. Abri a porta da escola, que estava emperrada. Vim subindo as escadas, não tinha mais parede, não tinha mais telhado, não tinha mais o auditório, que é uma das salas onde nós recebíamos todos os alunos para comemorar", conta.

Daiane lamenta que a escola tenha sido atingida justamente no ano de seu centenário, mas aposta exatamente na história da instituição para reunir a força e a resiliências necessárias para a reconstrução.

"É um momento de muita tristeza. São 100 anos de história e comemoramos muito dentro da nossa escola. Se aconteceu conosco no ano do centenário, então é porque a gente tem força para continuar e reerguer a nossa escola de novo, porque a nossa comunidade escolar merece."

Nesta terça-feira, a chuva voltou a atingir Tupanciretã , enquanto a cidade ainda se recupera dos temporais no fim da semana passada. A previsão de mais chuva preocupa os moradores. A orientação da prefeitura é que a população não tente subir nos telhados das casas para fazer reparos.

articles.title: Inflation: How rising food prices are squeezing Indian households
articles.summary: India's food inflation is broadening, squeezing household budgets.
articles.body:
India's inflation is rising again. And the biggest worry is what's happening to food prices.

The latest government data shows retail inflation climbed to 6.09% in October, up from 5.54% in September.

But look more closely at food inflation. It has surged to 8.94%.

The squeeze was sharper in rural India, where food inflation was 9.09%, compared with 8.68% in urban areas.

In other words, food prices are rising considerably faster than the overall rate of inflation.

Food inflation this year has been driven by a combination of weather disruptions, supply shortages and rising input costs, say economists.

With nearly 60% of its farmland dependent on rainfall , India remains acutely vulnerable to the vagaries of the monsoon. This year, the southwest monsoon was 13% below normal and unevenly distributed, while intensifying El Niño conditions have heightened risks to farm production.

A survey by polling agency LocalCircles found that six in 10 consumers say household essentials cost them over 20% more each month than a year ago, prompting calls for government intervention.

Rising prices are also forcing cutbacks: 74% are curbing discretionary spending on eating out, shopping and entertainment, while half are buying smaller quantities of essentials.

Food accounts for a smaller share of Indian household spending than it once did, but remains the biggest driver of inflation, with significant economic, social and political consequences.

In India's latest consumer price index, food and beverages account for 36.75% of the basket of goods and services used to measure inflation.

That is down sharply from 45.86% under the previous series, reflecting changing consumption patterns as Indians spend more on services, transport, healthcare, education and other non-food items.

Yet a sharp increase in food prices can move the overall inflation rate significantly, while disproportionately affecting people whose incomes leave little room for adjustment.

"Adjustability for a poor country like India is significantly lower," says Rajeswari Sengupta, an associate professor of economics at Mumbai-based Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research, pointing to the fact that a substantial proportion of household income is still spent on food.

According to calculations by Dharmakirti Joshi, chief economist at analytics firm Crisil, the bottom 20% of rural households faced inflation of 6.9% in October, against 6.5% for the richest 20%.

In urban India, the corresponding rates were 6.1% and 5.3%.

The pressure is visible even in the cost of a simple meal.

Crisil's Roti Rice Rate analysis found that the cost of a home-cooked vegetarian thali - a meal platter - rose 12% year-on-year in October, driven by higher prices of onions, tomatoes, vegetables, edible oil, rice and cooking gas. A non-vegetarian thali became 9% more expensive.

Rice prices were up about 10% year-on-year, pulses 8%, edible oil 13% and LPG 10%, according to Pushan Sharma, director of intelligence at Crisil. "It's no longer a few commodities that are driving this increase, it's becoming a little more broad-based," he says.

When onion prices spike, households can cut back on their consumption to some extent. But substituting rice, pulses and cooking oil is considerably harder.

And food inflation is not just about what farmers produce. It is also about how efficiently that food is stored, processed and moved to the market. Weaknesses at each stage can turn seasonal shortages into sharp price spikes - and gluts into waste.

Onions, for instance, are particularly susceptible to seasonal price swings.

The rabi crop - winter crops, sown after the monsoon and harvested in spring - which accounts for roughly two-thirds of onion production, is harvested in March and April and stored for several months. As stocks dwindle, prices can rise sharply before the next crop arrives.

Tomatoes, meanwhile, tend to see price spikes during the summer months, when arrivals decline in some markets or heat stress affects production.

Sharma says perishables are often responsible for the sudden spikes in food inflation, while prices of staples such as rice and wheat tend to rise more gradually but can stay higher for longer.

"The perishables are what caused the volatility. The non-perishables, like rice and wheat, are the ones that structurally increase the cost," he says.

Economists say India still lacks adequate infrastructure to sort, grade, store and process much of its perishable produce.

Tomatoes, for example, can become so abundant during a glut that farmers struggle to sell them at remunerative prices, only for consumers to face sharply higher prices months later.

Better storage and processing could help turn some of that surplus into products such as puree, smoothing the extremes between abundance and scarcity, according to Sharma

Energy shocks feed into the cost of transport, irrigation and agricultural inputs. Fertiliser prices can rise. Global edible-oil markets matter because India relies heavily on imports.

To be true, India, however, has some protection against the worst effects of food inflation.

Government stocks of cereals are comfortably above prescribed minimum levels, and the free-food programme covering nearly 800 million people offers a cushion against rising prices. Rice stocks are particularly ample.

There is a wider economic risk, says Sengupta.

"Food inflation may begin with a supply shock, but its effects can spread. Workers who find that their wages no longer cover basic living costs may seek higher pay. Businesses facing higher labour costs may raise prices. What begins as a rise in the price of food can gradually become a more general inflationary pressure - the familiar wage-price spiral that central banks try to prevent," she says.

For India, this creates a particularly difficult balancing act.

Agriculture is a relatively low-productivity sector, and the government has long sought to protect farmers by setting minimum support prices (MSPs) for certain crops - a price floor at which it promises to buy produce, helping farmers guard against a market crash.

At the same time, food prices are politically sensitive. Sharp increases in the price of staples such as onions and tomatoes can quickly anger consumers, prompting governments to step in with measures such as restricting exports, limiting how much traders can stockpile, or otherwise trying to bring prices down.

The broader story of India's changing food consumption makes the current inflation more interesting.

Households are eating differently from a decade ago. An analysis of the 2011-12 and 2023-24 consumption surveys shows that the share of cereals in food spending has fallen sharply, particularly among the poorest households, reflecting the impact of subsidised food programmes.

Meanwhile, consumption of nutrient-rich foods such as dairy, fruit and meat has increased across income groups, with the biggest gains among the poorest, the study revealed.

India's food basket is becoming more diverse. But diversity is meaningful only if ordinary Indians can afford it. Ultimately, food inflation is about what makes it to the plate - and what has to be left out.

articles.title: A Guernsey couple digging beneath their driveway uncover a hidden Nazi bunker dating back to World War II, complete with German messages on the walls and an escape hatch
articles.summary: A Guernsey couple made an unexpected discovery beneath their driveway while carrying out renovation work at their home, uncovering a sealed Nazi bunker
articles.body: A Guernsey couple made an unexpected discovery beneath their driveway while carrying out renovation work at their home, uncovering a sealed Nazi bunker dating back to the Second World War. Shaun and Carrie Tullier had known that their property stood on the site of a former German gun emplacement, but a tip from a previous resident led them to investigate what lay underground. Their excavation revealed two hidden rooms containing German wartime messages, old tins, a tiled floor and an escape hatch. Sealed since the 1960s, the bunker had remained out of sight for decades. The couple now hope to convert the historic structure into a games room and gym while preserving its original wartime features.How a hidden Nazi bunker was discovered beneath a Guernsey homeAs reported by the BBC, the Tulliers bought their home in the Torteval area of Guernsey four years before the discovery was reported in August 2025. They were aware of the site's military history, but information shared by a former occupant in March 2022 gave them a reason to look beneath the property.The previous resident suggested that a German bunker could still be buried underneath the house. Shaun had already noticed that the ground outside appeared to sit above another structure. With renovation work taking place at the property, he decided to investigate rather than leave the possibility unexplored. He hired a digger and began removing earth from the driveway with help from a friend. The excavation continued until the ground eventually gave way, revealing a doorway into the underground structure. What had been hidden beneath the property for years was now accessible again.What the couple found inside the hidden German bunkerThe bunker contained two principal rooms. One measured approximately 17ft by 10ft (5.18m by 3m), while the other was around 17ft by 20ft (5.18m by 6m). Despite having remained closed for decades, several features of the original structure were still visible. Inside, the couple found a tiled floor, an escape hatch and German writing on the walls. One inscription read "achtung feind hort mit", a German warning that translates as "beware, the enemy is listening". Other German phrases were also found around the interior, offering a glimpse of the building's original military use.There were also dozens of old tins and assorted debris left behind. The entrance is believed to have been sealed during the 1960s, leaving the bunker inaccessible for much of the period since the war.Guernsey couple to turn hidden World War II bunker into games room and gymThe discovery brought its own practical challenges. Water had accumulated inside the bunker over the years, making pumping and clearing the rooms among the first tasks. Shaun said he was surprised by the quality of the construction and described the structure as being in relatively sound condition. The couple have been working towards giving the space a new purpose. Their plans include a games room with a snooker table, alongside a gym. However, they do not intend to strip away the features that connect the building to its wartime past.The bunker has attracted interest from people curious about Guernsey's history, with visitors asking to see the underground rooms. Shaun said the couple wanted to preserve the German elements rather than simply convert the space into another part of their home.He has also spoken about the importance of retaining the structure as a reminder of what happened on the island during the occupation. While some people might prefer to demolish old military bunkers, the Tulliers said they felt fortunate to have discovered one beneath their property.How German forces turned the Channel Islands into a wartime fortressThe bunker dates back to a period when the Channel Islands were under German control. German forces occupied Guernsey and Jersey in 1940, retaining control until their liberation in May 1945. Under Adolf Hitler's orders, the islands were developed into a heavily fortified defensive position, intended to protect against an Allied invasion.The occupation brought severe hardships for local residents. Hundreds of islanders were deported to prisons across Europe, while those who remained faced food shortages and increasingly difficult living conditions. Alderney experienced particularly extensive disruption, with much of its population forced to leave their homes during the occupation. Guernsey and Jersey were liberated on 9 May 1945, followed by Sark a day later. Alderney's residents were not able to return until 15 December that year.You use AI every day. articles.body: In 2020, Sneha Joy from Kerala's Ernakulam district contested the local body elections as a United Democratic Front (UDF) candidate but lost by 13 votes. Little did she know that a new beginning was waiting for her. She moved to Canada and five years later she won the Canadian $5 million lottery jackpot, which is nearly Rs 30 crore! Sneha, a woman from Kerala's Ernakulam district, won in Canada’s Lotto 6/49 lottery, turning an ordinary lottery ticket into a life-changing windfall.Let’s find out more about this lucky woman:Meet Sneha JoySneha is originally from Vengoor near Perumbavoor in Kerala. Her journey from local politics to becoming a millionaire in Canada has made headlines. articles.title: 26 seats vs 120 demand: Why Saharanpur, Gandhi family turfs are testing Congress-SP ties
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Differences over seat-sharing have surfaced between the Congress and Samajwadi Party ahead of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Differences over seat-sharing have surfaced between the Congress and Samajwadi Party ahead of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. The Congress is demanding 120 constituencies, including the Gandhi family's traditional strongholds of Amethi and Raebareli, and is unwilling to settle for fewer seats, news agency ANI reported, citing party sources.Congress conveyed its demand during a meeting with SP leaders in Delhi, where it submitted a list of 120 constituencies it wants to contest, sources told ANI.The list reportedly includes two seats in Saharanpur, where the SP has already announced its candidates, as well as several constituencies in traditional Congress stronghold Raebareli and Amethi, some of which have sitting SP MLAs.What SP has said on Amethi, RaebareliOn the Congress staking a claim to Amethi and Raebareli, Samajwadi Party leader SP Singh Patel has asserted that the majority of seats in the two neighbouring districts should go to the Akhilesh-led party, arguing that the SP has sitting MLAs there while the Congress does not."Naturally, the party that holds the sitting MLA seats should get them. Furthermore, our own party workers and other leaders have done excellent work, and they deserve to be considered. Therefore, in both Rae Bareli and Amethi, the majority -- or rather, almost all -- of the seats should go to the Samajwadi Party," Patel said.The grand old party's proposed list reportedly includes several constituencies in the Raebareli and Amethi districts, some of which are currently represented by Samajwadi Party MLAs. The demand could emerge as another point of contention between the two parties during their seat-sharing negotiations.Why Amethi and Raebareli matterAmethi and Raebareli have long been considered the Gandhi family's political turf, with both constituencies playing a significant role in the family's electoral legacy.Amethi's association with the Gandhi family began with Sanjay Gandhi, who won the Lok Sabha seat in 1980. After his death, his brother Rajiv Gandhi won the constituency three consecutive times. The seat later passed to Sonia Gandhi, who won it in 1999 on her political entry, before handing it over to her son Rahul Gandhi.Rahul won Amethi three times, in 2004, 2009 and 2014, before losing to BJP's actor-turned-politician Smriti Irani in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections.Raebareli, meanwhile, has been associated with the family since the first-ever Lok Sabha elections in 1952, when Feroze Gandhi won the seat. He retained it in 1957 as well. After his death, his wife and former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi represented the constituency, winning in 1967, 1971 and 1980.The seat remained with the family from 2004 onwards, with Sonia Gandhi winning it in four consecutive Lok Sabha elections before making way for Rahul Gandhi, who won Raebareli in the 2024 general elections.While the upcoming contest is for the Uttar Pradesh assembly and not the Lok Sabha, the seats in these two districts continue to hold symbolic significance for the Gandhi family.SP stresses on 'winnability'Meanwhile, SP supremo Akhilesh Yadav has stressed that "winnability" and the larger objective of defeating the BJP should guide the seat-sharing arrangement.In a post on X, Akhilesh called for mutual understanding between the alliance partners and said candidates should be selected based on their electoral prospects. He also emphasised the need for consensus candidates representing the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework on every seat to take on the BJP.The differences have also triggered sharp reactions within the Congress. Saharanpur MP Imran Masood questioned the SP's reported offer of just 26 seats to the Congress, asking, "Are we beggars?"While the Congress has drawn a line at 120 seats, Akhilesh has indicated that discussions should continue, with the focus on identifying candidates capable of winning rather than dividing constituencies strictly between the two parties.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bengaluru man relocates from Chennai, pays Voltas Rs 1,770 to reinstall AC, technicians damage it during reinstallation, consumer commission orders Voltas to pay Rs 33,770 compensation
articles.summary: BENGALURU: A Bengaluru consumer commission has directed Voltas Ltd to pay Rs 33,770 to a customer after finding deficiency in service by its technicians,
articles.body: BENGALURU: A Bengaluru consumer commission has directed Voltas Ltd to pay Rs 33,770 to a customer after finding deficiency in service by its technicians, who allegedly damaged his air conditioner while reinstalling it after he relocated from Chennai.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (Bengaluru Urban) directed the company to pay Rs 25,000 as consolidated compensation for the damage and operational loss of the AC, along with 3% annual interest from the date of filing the complaint.It also ordered a refund of Rs 1,770 towards installation charges, Rs 5,000 for mental agony and harassment, and Rs 2,000 towards litigation expenses.The commission directed Voltas to comply with the order within 45 days.According to the complaint filed by S Balaji, 37, his Voltas 1.5-tonne split AC (Model 183SY) was in working condition when it was dismantled in Chennai in March 2025. A technical fitness report issued by Dynamic Cool Center had certified that the unit was functional before it was moved to Bengaluru.After relocating, Balaji approached Voltas for reinstallation on April 19, 2025, and paid Rs 1,770 for the service. He alleged that the technicians deployed by the company lacked the necessary expertise and leaked the entire refrigerant gas charge during the installation process, leaving the machine non-functional.The complaint stated that Voltas technicians returned on May 1 and refilled the refrigerant gas without charging him. However, Balaji alleged that they left the cooling system unpressurised and exposed, allowing atmospheric moisture to enter over the next 12 days. This allegedly damaged the printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) and fan motor.Despite raising multiple service requests and escalating the matter through emails, the AC developed recurring reset problems and eventually stopped functioning completely. Balaji also approached the National Consumer Helpline, but his grievances were marked as disposed of without a technical resolution.The commission noted that the complainant had submitted documents establishing that the AC was functional before its relocation and that it developed major defects following the reinstallation carried out by Voltas. It also observed that the company had failed to provide any contrary technical evidence or written explanation." The deployment of untrained staff and the subsequent terminal damage to the machine amounts to a deficiency of service," the commission observed.However, it declined to award the full original purchase value of Rs 33,000 sought by Balaji, noting that the AC was not brand new when it was reinstalled in Bengaluru and had already been used in Chennai. It said awarding the full purchase value without accounting for depreciation would be inequitable.The commission, comprising president Ramachandra M S and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani, passed the order on September 30, 2026. articles.title: Luton's Asian women 'never heard' on health, says centre director
articles.summary: Women react to a report saying poor female health in Luton develops five years earlier than average.
articles.body:
A community centre director in Luton said a "hidden generation" of Asian women had "voices that were never heard" when it came to their wellbeing.

The Let Women Speak report commissioned by the borough council in Luton, where the onset of poor female health happens five years earlier than average, also found over 70% of women aged 45-64 had an at-risk body mass index.

Firoza Abdool-Sathar, director of the Centre for Youth and Community Development (CYCD), said: "Some of our ladies maybe 20 years ago, their voices did not matter.

"These were ladies in Luton, especially the South Asian population, with family dynamics, the lack of opportunities, economic inactivity and language barriers as well."

Luton's population is around 236,000 according to the Office for National Statistics and more than half belong to ethnic minority groups, including strong Pakistani and Bangladeshi communities.

More than 250 people of different ages and cultures were interviewed for the report, which focused on the 112,400 women and girls in the town.

It found only 52.5% of women aged 25-49 took up cervical screening and only 63% underwent breast screening, compared to 71% nationally.

Following the report, councillors have agreed to champion women's health and support measures to improve wellbeing.

Based in Bury Park, where over 70% of the population identifies as Asian, those CYCD supports include victims of unhealthy relationships, domestic abuse and survivors of female genital mutilation.

Abdool-Sathar, who is in her late 50s, said: "When you look at older people the stats haven't improved, in fact, it's gotten worse for a lot of women.

"These stories are only coming out now and we're only understanding the scale of the problem.

"A lot don't go for preventative methods whether it's contraceptives or getting themselves checked in advance, or just feel something niggling at them, whereas people in more affluent areas will have that luxury and time."

She hoped things were improving for future generations.

"Girls nowadays, they've become much better, more educated, so they've got lots more opportunities and use that as an impetus to continue and better their lives."

Her colleague at CYCD, Yasmin Akhtar Yasin, 47, project co-ordinator for the "End The Silence", said there was still stigma around some health issues.

"Do I tell someone I'm depressed if I'm going to be put on antidepressants?

"We have struggles every day and are known to be multitaskers, us women. So do we put our health before our children, our in-laws, our mums, our mothers-in-law, our husbands, and can we hold a job down?

She felt for some women, lack of education, especially for those where English is their second language, could be a barrier.

"It could be any woman with any colour, any status, but she doesn't realise why she's having a hard time at work at the moment. Menopause? What is that?

"Her life can be wonderful one day and then she wakes up and doesn't know why she hasn't slept, her hot and cold flushes.

"Is she getting support from work or her GP? Or her partner and family, who now decide she's the crazy one."

With gym memberships not affordable to all, the CYCD runs exercise and wellbeing activities.

Another woman, 45, who regularly attends the centre but asked not to be named, said things changed when she married for love and started raising her five children over a 15-year period.

"Once I got married, I was moulded into something where I couldn't speak up and lost my confidence.

"I had to make food for my in-laws, my husband and kids and do household duties. You don't think about your health, you carry on, you carry on, you carry on, until your body's shutting down, and that's what happened to me.

"I wake up in the morning with anxiety and it takes a few hours to calm down, but it still comes back."

She said she was now able to spend an hour a day doing exercise, which helped deal with her panic attacks.

"I'm struggling with that every single day, but at least feel I'm doing something in life.

"I've been feeling better in myself but those years have affected my body, my joints and everything has been affected so I'm living with it and struggling."

articles.title: Navy, Coast Guard helicopter acquisition puts Leonardo, Airbus and HAL in focus
articles.summary: The Indian navy and coast guard are preparing to acquire 76 Naval Utility Helicopters (NUHs) in a procurement programme estimated at around Rs 15,000
articles.body: The Indian navy and coast guard are preparing to acquire 76 Naval Utility Helicopters (NUHs) in a procurement programme estimated at around Rs 15,000 crore, with European manufacturers expected to emerge as the front-runners. The requirement comprises 51 helicopters for the navy and 25 for the coast guard, and is aimed at replacing the ageing Chetak fleet.The purchase is likely to be made under the Buy and Make (Indian) category, which would require foreign original equipment manufacturers to team up with Indian companies for domestic production. The helicopters will be expected to handle maritime surveillance, reconnaissance, search and rescue, casualty evacuation and the transport of personnel and cargo. Operating from warships adds further demands, including limited deck space, folding rotor blades and the ability to withstand harsh sea conditions.Among the possible contenders is Leonardo's AW169M. Italian firm Leonardo has announced a partnership with Adani Defence and Aerospace in February 2026 to build a helicopter manufacturing and maintenance ecosystem in India. The AW169M has been identified as one of the platforms for local production. The twin-engine machine has wheeled landing gear, folding main rotor blades and a compact layout suited to shipboard use, for easier stowage in the tight spaces on a ship.Airbus Helicopters' H160M could also be in the running, though its weight may prove a hurdle. The military version is designed for troop transport, reconnaissance, special operations and armed missions, while its civilian predecessor has experience in offshore transport and search and rescue. Airbus could draw on its industrial tie-up with Tata Advanced Systems for local manufacturing. However, the helicopter's published maximum take-off weight of around 6,050 kg is above the 5,500 kg ceiling set in the August 2025 request for information, which could complicate its eligibility.Hindustan Aeronautics Limited's Utility Helicopter-Maritime, developed specifically for naval operations, is another option. It is expected to have folding rotor blades, strengthened landing gear, corrosion protection and emergency flotation equipment. Its reported design weight of about 5.7 tonnes, however, also exceeds the RFI limit. The Navy is separately pursuing 60 UH-M helicopters, which is a distinct requirement from the 76 NUHs.Leonardo's AW109 TrekkerM and Bell Textron's Bell 429 are other possible alternatives, though both would need closer scrutiny of their naval configurations. The AW109 TrekkerM uses skid landing gear in its standard form, while the Bell 429 is available with wheels. Shipboard compatibility, folding rotor arrangements and maritime operational qualifications would remain key questions for both.The two forces will have differing priorities as the navy needs helicopters that can operate from frigates, destroyers and other warships, while the coast guard is likely to focus on maritime surveillance, search and rescue, medical evacuation and law enforcement support. The programme also comes amid a wider helicopter modernisation drive, with the Army and the IAF pursuing 400 light utility helicopters.

articles.title: A man named two relatives as beneficiaries of a $746,000 life insurance policy during Idaho divorce proceedings, then died in a mining accident; on November 23, judges revived his wife's claim to a share
articles.summary: A life insurance policy became the centre of a legal dispute after a man changed its beneficiaries while his divorce was pending and subsequently died in
articles.body: A life insurance policy became the centre of a legal dispute after a man changed its beneficiaries while his divorce was pending and subsequently died in a mining accident. Although his estranged wife was not named on the policy, she argued that she was entitled to half of its proceeds because the insurance benefits were part of their marital property.In a November 23, 2026, decision in Ashlock v. Ashlock, the US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit vacated a federal court judgment favouring the deceased man's relatives and reopened the wife's legal challenge. The ruling, available on Justia, held that a federal law exception allowing certain divorce-related orders to override Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) preemption can apply to employer-sponsored life insurance plans as well as pension plans. The court sent the case back for further proceedings to determine whether the wife's court orders qualify for that protection.Husband named relatives as beneficiaries during divorceTina Ashlock and Jerry Ashlock married in 2009. Jerry filed for divorce in an Idaho state court in December 2020. During the proceedings, the court issued an injunction prohibiting either spouse from transferring property acquired during their marriage while the divorce case remained pending.In March 2021, Jerry started working for Stillwater Mining Company in Montana and enrolled in an employer-sponsored life insurance policy issued by Life Insurance Company of North America (LINA). Despite the injunction, he named his relatives, Mary Ashlock and Brad Wilt, as the policy's only beneficiaries.Jerry died in a mining accident in Montana in June 2021, before the divorce was finalised. Tina subsequently contacted LINA, claiming an interest in the insurance proceeds. The insurer rejected her claim because she was not named as a beneficiary and argued that ERISA prevented her from claiming the money under state community-property laws. In December 2021, LINA confirmed that it had distributed the entire $746,000 policy payout to Mary and Brad.State courts recognised wife's 50% interestTina continued pursuing her claim through state courts. In September 2022, an Idaho court issued an order recognising her 50% community-property interest in the insurance proceeds. It also found that Jerry had violated the divorce-related injunction by naming his relatives as beneficiaries. The Idaho court deferred enforcement of Tina's interest to the Montana probate court, which subsequently adopted the findings and conclusions of the Idaho order and recognised her community-property interest.Tina then filed a federal lawsuit against Mary, Brad, LINA and Principal Life Insurance Company. She sought a declaration recognising her entitlement to the proceeds and alleged unjust enrichment against the two relatives. She also brought an ERISA claim against the insurer, alleging that it had improperly denied her benefits. However, in July 2024, the US District Court for the District of Arizona dismissed her claim against LINA. It later entered judgment in favour of Mary and Brad, agreeing with the argument that ERISA's exception for qualified domestic relations orders applied only to pension plans, not life insurance policies.Appeals court explains how QDRO protection appliesTina challenged the federal court's decision before the Ninth Circuit. The central question was whether ERISA's qualified domestic relations order (QDRO) exception could cover welfare benefit plans, including employer-sponsored life insurance. A QDRO is a domestic relations order that recognises another person's right to receive some or all of the benefits under an employee benefit plan. Such orders can protect a spouse's or former spouse's interests in benefits during divorce proceedings.The appeals court explained that ERISA recognises both pension plans and welfare benefit plans. The latter include employer-sponsored benefits providing accident, disability and death coverage. The judges held that the statutory language does not restrict the QDRO exception to pension plans. They also noted that several other federal appeals courts had previously reached the same interpretation.Ninth Circuit sends case back for further proceedingsThe Ninth Circuit vacated the federal district court's judgment and remanded the case for further proceedings. It instructed the lower court to determine whether Tina possesses a qualifying QDRO that entitles her to a share of the insurance proceeds.The November 23 ruling does not itself award Tina half of the $746,000 or order Mary and Brad to return the money. Instead, it establishes that the QDRO exception can apply to the type of life insurance plan involved, allowing her claim to be considered under the correct interpretation of federal law.You use AI every day. articles.title: Stunning images capture Brazil’s Christ the Redeemer statue floating above a sea of clouds
articles.summary: Images and videos showing Brazil's iconic Christ the Redeemer statue rising above a thick layer of clouds have gone viral on social media, with many
articles.body: Images and videos showing Brazil's iconic Christ the Redeemer statue rising above a thick layer of clouds have gone viral on social media, with many viewers questioning whether the visuals are real.Images and videos show the over 30-metre-tall statue on Corcovado Mountain in Rio de Janeiro standing above dense white clouds covering the slopes below. Some aerial views show the monument surrounded by what appears to be a sea of clouds, while other shots capture it emerging above the cloud cover with parts of the city visible in the foreground.The visuals were captured by Brazilian audiovisual specialist Marcio Amaro and photographer Andrés, who is known online as andreslpaez. The images and videos document a weather phenomenon in which clouds cover the lower slopes of the mountain while leaving its summit exposed.The phenomenon, known as orographic lift, occurs when moist air from the Atlantic Ocean is forced upwards as it encounters the 710-metre-high Corcovado Mountain. As the air rises, it cools and condenses, forming low clouds and fog. These can cover parts of the mountain and the surrounding city while the summit remains clear.Christ the Redeemer, completed in 1931, stands within Tijuca National Park and overlooks Rio de Janeiro and Guanabara Bay. The statue is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Watch: Bangladesh’s Grameen Bank faces a wave of arson; 100 attacks in 15 days
articles.summary: Bangladesh’s renewed political unrest over former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s planned return has spilled into a wave of arson and attacks on
articles.body: Bangladesh’s renewed political unrest over former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s planned return has spilled into a wave of arson and attacks on institutions linked to her political rivals.Grameen Bank, founded by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, who led the interim government after Hasina’s ouster, has been among the targets, with the bank recording 100 incidents of arson or attempted arson at its branches and offices since November 10.The bank’s Internal Audit and Compliance Division report, dated November 24, lists incidents across the country. It includes an attack on the Patgati branch in Tungipara, which was targeted twice, on November 10 and 15.In the latest incidents, attackers hurled petrol bombs at branches in Lalmonirhat and Tangail in the early hours of Tuesday. At the Patgram branch in Lalmonirhat, a petrol bomb was thrown at the veranda around 2.45am. The night guard and branch manager raised the alarm, forcing the attackers to flee. The report said there was no major damage, though a halogen light temporarily went out.At the Shashanpur branch in Gopalpur, Tangail, another petrol bomb was thrown around 2am, damaging the branch’s signboard.The tally has risen from 97 incidents recorded in the bank’s previous report, dated November 23. It includes attempted attacks that caused little or no damage.Branches damaged, records destroyedThe attacks have also disrupted operations and damaged records at several branches.At the Ulpur branch in Gopalganj, attackers set fire to the office on November 15, burning collection sheets and damaging a table. They also broke CCTV equipment and took a hard disk, according to the bank’s incident record.In another attack on November 23, two people poured petrol near the main gate of the Keroa Raipur branch in Noakhali and set it alight. A night guard and a peon extinguished the fire before it spread. Police later examined CCTV footage and arrested one person, the report said.An earlier attack on the Kashiani branch in Gopalganj on November 18 caused extensive damage. Branch manager Solaiman Morol told Al Jazeera that around a dozen men arrived carrying machetes, petrol and tools to break locks. They looted the office and tried to cut open its vault with a grinder.The attackers took about 40 sacks of vouchers and other documents and burned them, Morol said. They also stole office furniture and equipment. The branch has been unable to resume normal operations, while staff have received threats and customers have expressed concern about their deposits and loan records.Morol said the attackers claimed that destroying the records would mean borrowers no longer had to repay their loans.Yunus seeks international helpThe latest report came a day after Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus appealed to the international community to help stop what he described as a “calculated campaign of arson and terror” against the bank.Yunus said branches had been attacked with petrol bombs almost daily since the beginning of November, often accompanied by slogans associated with the Awami League, the party of ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina.He called for those responsible to be brought to justice and urged supporters of the bank around the world to help stop the attacks. He also said Grameen Bank had asked the Ministry of Home Affairs for stronger security.The violence has raised concerns over the safety of the bank’s employees and borrowers. Grameen Bank has around 21,000 employees and about 11 million borrowers, most of them women, according to figures cited by Yunus and the bank.The institution is owned 90% by its borrower-members, with the government holding the remaining 10%. The attacks therefore threaten not only the bank’s operations but also the financial security of millions of rural borrowers who rely on it for credit and savings.Political tensions surround the attacksBangladesh’s government has blamed the Awami League for the attacks. The violence has come amid renewed political activity by Hasina’s supporters, months after she was ousted in August 2024 and Yunus stepped down as chief adviser.Political analysts cited by Al Jazeera said Grameen Bank had become a symbol of Yunus and a target for supporters of the former prime minister. Some viewed the attacks as an attempt to demonstrate that the Awami League still had a presence on the streets, despite being barred from electoral politics.The government has rejected suggestions that it is unable to contain the violence.Police headquarters told Al Jazeera that eight cases had been filed and eight people arrested in connection with the attacks.Grameen Bank managing director Sarder Akhter Hamed said police had responded when the bank sought help and had sometimes warned it of possible attacks. However, he said staff had largely been left to remain alert and protect themselves.The attacks have also drawn alarm from human rights organisations, which warned that the violence puts bank workers and members at risk and threatens the economic rights of women entrepreneurs and rural communities.You use AI every day. articles.title: A rare uncut sheet of 110 holographic Pokémon cards from 1999, including Dragonite and Gengar, was found rolled up in a family attic in England, and it could fetch up to £10,000 at auction on November 29
articles.summary: One family's forgotten bundle in the attic for almost 30 years may be their most valuable find.
articles.body: One family's forgotten bundle in the attic for almost 30 years may be their most valuable find. The 110 uncut holographic cards in an old trading card roll were a rare Pokemon collectible. Now, as nostalgia for the franchise continues to attract collectors, the unusual find is heading to auction with an estimated value reaching £10,000.According to SWNS, the Surrey family discovered the collection while clearing out their loft. This sheet from the 1999 Pokémon Fossil expansion is a rare alternative to collectors' album single cards.A rare piece of Pokémon historyThe English-language sheet contains 110 holographic cards featuring 15 different Pokémon, including popular characters Dragonite and Gengar.According to Your Local Guardian, the collection had remained rolled up and stored in the family's attic since it was acquired decades ago. Its origins can be traced to a relative of the owner who worked for KB Toys, an American toy retailer, during the 1990s and early 2000s.The family reportedly did not initially recognise the potential value of the material. Growing interest in Pokémon collectibles eventually prompted them to seek professional advice, leading to its identification as a rare auction item.Auctioneers at Cullens of Surrey have placed an estimated value of between £6,000 and £10,000 on the sheet. National World reported that the unusual format is a major attraction, as collectors generally encounter these holographic designs as separately cut trading cards rather than as part of an original production sheet.Condition and auction detailsDespite surviving for almost 30 years, the sheet is not entirely free from damage. Your Local Guardian reported that its condition includes scratches, residue, creasing and a tear on the reverse side.Prospective buyers will be able to examine detailed photographs and a condition report before placing their bids, allowing them to assess the extent of the wear.The collection will feature in Cullens of Surrey Auctions' largest-ever Toy, Model and Trading Card Sale, scheduled for Sunday, November 29, at 3pm. According to SWNS, the auction will offer collectors an opportunity to acquire an unusual piece of the franchise's late-1990s trading card history.The event will be conducted entirely online through a live webcast, with no in-room bidding. National World reported that advance online bidding opened on November 20, giving interested buyers an opportunity to participate before the main sale.Other collectibles heading under the hammerThe Pokémon sheet is not the only notable item expected to attract attention. The auction also includes a complete first-edition Fossil Pokémon card set in near-mint condition, alongside other complete and partially complete collections.According to National World, a separate complete set of 62 Fossil expansion cards carries an estimate of up to £2,500, while an individual Snorlax card could reach £2,000.Sports memorabilia will also feature, including a 2000 trading card of American football star Tom Brady. articles.title: Chhattisgarh HC recalculates doctor's accident compensation, cuts award by Rs 12 lakh over tax deduction error, rules income tax must be deducted as per applicable slabs
articles.summary: RAIPUR: The Chhattisgarh high court has reduced the compensation awarded to the family of a doctor killed in a road accident by Rs 12.13 lakh after
articles.body: RAIPUR: The Chhattisgarh high court has reduced the compensation awarded to the family of a doctor killed in a road accident by Rs 12.13 lakh after holding that the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) had incorrectly calculated income tax deductions while assessing his annual income. However, the court upheld the tribunal's decision to grant 30% towards future prospects, rejecting the insurance company's plea to reduce it to 25%.Justice Santosh Sharma, while partly allowing an appeal filed by New India Assurance Company Limited on Nov 23, modified the compensation from Rs 2,49,46,800 to Rs 2,37,33,211, along with applicable interest.The case relates to the death of Indrajeet Singh Siddhu, a 49-year-old professional consultant in the Department of General Medicine at a private hospital in Korba. He died on June 5, 2017, when the car in which he was travelling from Bilaspur to Korba collided with a capsule truck near RTO village Lagra in Bilaspur district. The truck was allegedly being driven at high speed and negligently.Siddhu, who was earning Rs 2.30 lakh per month (Rs 27.60 lakh annually), died on the spot. His widow and two children subsequently approached the MACT, seeking compensation of Rs 3.27 crore.In Jan 2020, the tribunal awarded them Rs 2,49,46,800 with 7.5% annual interest. While calculating the compensation, it deducted 20% towards income tax, added 30% for future prospects and applied a multiplier of 13 after deducting one-third towards personal and living expenses.Challenging the award, the insurance company argued that the tribunal had wrongly deducted only 20% towards income tax, whereas the applicable tax rate for the financial year 2017-18 was 30% on income exceeding Rs 10 lakh, in addition to the applicable cess. It contended that the compensation should be reduced to Rs 2,28,23,094. The insurer also argued that future prospects should be restricted to 25% considering the deceased's age.Examining the income tax slabs applicable for 2017-18, the High Court calculated the total tax liability on Siddhu's annual income of Rs 27.60 lakh at Rs 6,59,715, including cess. Consequently, his net annual income after tax was determined at Rs 21,00,285, instead of the Rs 22,08,000 assessed by the tribunal.The court recalculated the loss of dependency at Rs 2,36,63,211 after adding 30% towards future prospects, deducting one-third towards personal expenses and applying the multiplier of 13. It retained the Rs 70,000 awarded under conventional heads, taking the total compensation to Rs 2,37,33,211.Rejecting the insurance company's argument for reducing future prospects to 25%, the court observed that the tribunal had treated the deceased as a salaried person after considering the nature of his employment and the material on record.Referring to the Supreme Court's ruling in National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi, the High Court held that a 30% addition towards future prospects was permissible for a person in permanent employment in the 40-50 age group.The court therefore partly allowed the insurance company's appeal, holding that the income tax deduction required correction but finding no error in the tribunal's approach towards future prospects.The remaining findings of the tribunal were left undisturbed.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: A North Carolina couple lost their 18-year-old daughter in a car crash; 22 years later, they are honouring her memory by rescuing hundreds of orphaned and injured animals through a wildlife centre named after her
articles.summary: A couple in North Carolina, US, have turned an unimaginable personal tragedy into a mission to protect wildlife.
articles.body: A couple in North Carolina, US, have turned an unimaginable personal tragedy into a mission to protect wildlife. Byron and Kim Wortham lost their 18-year-old daughter, Holly, in a car crash in February 2004. More than two decades later, they are keeping her memory alive through Holly's Nest Animal Rescue, a wildlife rehabilitation centre they established in her honour. The facility takes in injured, abandoned and orphaned animals, nurses them back to health and releases them into suitable natural habitats. From baby deer whose mothers have been killed on roads to injured owls, raccoons and foxes, the couple's work has grown into a demanding commitment to wildlife conservation, with the centre now caring for hundreds of animals each year.How the couple turned personal loss into a wildlife rescue missionHolly Wortham was 18 and in her final year of high school when she died in a car accident in February 2004. She was remembered by her family as an artist and an animal lover. Her death deeply affected her parents and their three other children.In the years that followed, Kim struggled with the loss and found it difficult to return to her previous routine. She eventually left her job at a library. Caring for animals gradually became a way for her to reconnect with the world and find purpose after the tragedy.Byron and Kim began obtaining the necessary permits to rehabilitate small mammals, including squirrels, rabbits and opossums. What started as an effort to honour Holly's affection for animals gradually developed into a dedicated wildlife rescue operation. They named it Holly's Nest to ensure that their daughter's memory remained at the centre of their work.What happens at Holly's Nest Animal RescueLocated near Sanford in Lee County, North Carolina, Holly's Nest is a wildlife rehabilitation facility that receives animals from members of the public, wildlife officers and other rehabilitators.Its work involves rescuing injured, abandoned and orphaned animals, providing medical attention and specialised care, and preparing them for release once they can survive independently.The centre looks after a wide range of native wildlife, including white-tailed deer, raccoons, foxes, opossums, squirrels, rabbits, beavers, owls, hawks and other birds. Some animals arrive with serious injuries, while others are too young to survive without human intervention.The facility has also cared for animals with unusual conditions, including an albino fawn, a dwarf raccoon and a disabled squirrel.Why orphaned fawns make up a major part of their workOne of the centre's biggest responsibilities is caring for white-tailed deer, particularly fawns separated from their mothers after road accidents. According to a June 2026 report by The News & Observer, Holly's Nest has become North Carolina's largest deer rehabilitation facility, taking in an average of around 150 fawns annually.During the busiest part of the season, the centre can receive five to eight new fawns a day for about a month. On June 5, 2026, approximately 50 fawns were being cared for at the facility.Some arrive in particularly distressing circumstances, including newborns whose mothers have been struck by vehicles shortly after giving birth. The young deer require regular bottle-feeding and close attention until they are strong enough to survive without human care.Their home has become an extension of the rescue centreThe Worthams' commitment to wildlife rehabilitation extends well beyond the centre's outdoor enclosures. Over the years, animals requiring special attention have also been cared for inside their home.A beaver named Bucky once occupied a bathtub in the bathroom that had belonged to Holly. He even attempted to build a dam there. Baby raccoons have been seen resting in hammocks, while young foxes have slept in dog beds. The couple has also cared for animals in their basement, particularly those requiring cooler conditions.The household has included two macaws named Jimmy Buffett and Bruce Springsteen. Kim has spoken about her affection for beavers, describing their behaviour as similar to that of children.These unusual arrangements reflect the demands of looking after animals that cannot immediately be placed in outdoor rehabilitation enclosures.Thousands of acres provide a place for rescued animals to returnRehabilitation is only one part of the couple's conservation work. Finding suitable habitats where recovered animals can be released is equally important.According to The News & Observer, Tim Sweeney, founder and CEO of Epic Games, provided Holly's Nest with access to approximately 8,000 acres of land for wildlife releases. The protected areas give rehabilitated animals an opportunity to return to natural surroundings rather than being released into unsuitable or heavily developed locations.The arrangement has been particularly valuable for animals that need appropriate habitat to survive independently. For the Worthams, the ultimate objective is not to keep rescued wildlife in captivity but to give it a chance to return to the wild.A demanding routine that can last 18 hours a dayRunning the rehabilitation centre requires considerable time and physical effort. During the busiest months, the couple can spend as many as 18 hours a day feeding animals, cleaning enclosures, preparing food and attending to new arrivals.April through October is particularly demanding because many young animals need assistance during this period. The couple prepares different diets depending on the species, with food including fruit, oats and other suitable provisions.Byron also takes their conservation message beyond the facility. He conducts wildlife education programmes at schools, parks, veterans' facilities and community venues, helping people understand the challenges faced by native animals.The centre's work is supported by donations, volunteers and the couple's own contributions. The 2024 report stated that Holly's Nest did not receive federal, state or local government funding and relied on donations and personal resources to meet its expenses.The goal is to return every animal to the wildDespite the care and attention the animals receive, the Worthams believe that successful rehabilitation should ultimately lead to freedom. Their aim is to help wildlife recover sufficiently to survive in its natural environment rather than remain dependent on humans.Byron has expressed this philosophy through a simple belief: "five minutes of freedom is better than a lifetime of captivity".The couple's work has therefore become more than a tribute to their daughter. Through Holly's Nest, they are helping injured and orphaned wildlife recover, while also giving animals that have lost their natural habitats or mothers another opportunity to survive.For Byron and Kim, every animal that returns to the wild represents another way of keeping Holly's love for nature alive.You use AI every day.
